History[edit]"Outagamie", a French transliteration of the 
Anishinaabe term for the 
Meskwaki (Fox) people, means "dwellers of the other shore" or "dwellers on the other side of the stream", 
[4]referring to their historic habitation along the 
St. Lawrence River and south of the Great Lakes. They occupied considerable territory in Wisconsin before colonization.
[5] Outagamie County was created in 1851 and organized in 1852.
[6] Before that, it was under the jurisdiction of 
Brown County.
